items.paragraph: Treatment emergence ends 14 days after the treatment end date, and that day is included in the window.
items.question: When does treatment emergence end?

alternatives.rule: Treatment emergence has no end date.
alternatives.meaning: Every event that starts on or after the start of treatment emergence is treatment-emergent, however long after the treatment end date (the on-study reading of the FDA guide).

alternatives.rule: Treatment emergence ends <days> days after the treatment end date, that day included.
alternatives.meaning: An event that starts later than that many days after the treatment end date is not treatment-emergent; one that starts on the last day of the window still is.

items.question: Which rows does the adverse event summary table have?

alternatives.rule: The rows of the adverse event summary table are any event, related events, serious events, serious related events, fatal events, and events leading to discontinuation of study treatment.
alternatives.meaning: The rows and their order are those of the ARS example "Common Safety Displays", output Out14-3-1-1, without its rows of related fatal events and of events leading to dose modification.

alternatives.rule: The rows of the adverse event summary table are, in this order, <rows>.
alternatives.meaning: Each row is named by its code: ANY, RELATED, SERIOUS, SERIOUS_RELATED (serious and related), DISCONTINUATION, DOSE_MODIFIED (leading to a dose reduction or an interruption), FATAL or FATAL_RELATED (fatal and related).

items.paragraph: An adverse event is treatment-emergent if it starts on or after the first dose; date and time are compared where both were collected, and dates alone are compared otherwise.
items.question: When does treatment emergence begin?

alternatives.rule: An adverse event is treatment-emergent when it starts on or after the treatment start date.
alternatives.meaning: Dates are compared; times are ignored.

alternatives.rule: An adverse event is treatment-emergent when it starts at or after the date and time of the first dose.
alternatives.meaning: A start or a first dose collected without a time counts from 00:00 of its day.

alternatives.rule: An adverse event is treatment-emergent when it starts on or after the first dose, comparing date and time where both were collected and dates otherwise.
alternatives.meaning: On the first dose date, an event is not treatment-emergent only when both its start time and the time of the first dose were collected and it starts before the dose; an event on that date without a collected time is treatment-emergent.

items.paragraph: The treatment end date is the latest start date among the exposure records that have a dose.
items.question: What is the treatment end date?

alternatives.rule: The treatment end date is the latest end date of an exposure record with a dose.
The treatment end date is the latest start date of an exposure record with a dose.
The treatment end date is the latest end date of an exposure record with a dose, or the end-of-study disposition date when no such record has an end date.
alternatives.meaning: The disposition date is the start date of the end-of-study record (decision disp.status.record). It is taken only for a subject with a treatment start.

alternatives.rule: The treatment end date is the latest end date of any exposure record.
alternatives.meaning: Every exposure record takes part, whatever its dose: the counterpart of trt.start.source/first_ex_record, for an EX in which EXDOSE is not populated (EXDOSE is not a Required variable of SDTMIG).

items.paragraph: Baseline body mass index is derived from baseline weight and height and is kept at full precision.
items.question: How is baseline body mass index obtained?

alternatives.rule: Baseline body mass index is derived from baseline weight and height, at full precision.
alternatives.meaning: Weight in kg divided by the square of height in m, with height collected in cm and divided by 100; weight in kg and height in cm are assumed. The value is kept at full precision: a table rounds it once, at display (PLAN.md section 7.2).

alternatives.rule: Baseline body mass index is the collected body mass index, selected by the rule for baseline weight and height.
alternatives.meaning: The collected value is the vital sign with VSTESTCD equal to BMI.

items.paragraph: The randomized set consists of every randomized subject.
items.question: Who is in the randomized set?

alternatives.rule: The randomized set holds every randomized subject.
alternatives.meaning: The randomized set is written to ITTFL: the FDA guide calls it the randomized population, often referred to as the intent-to-treat population.

alternatives.rule: The randomized set holds every randomized subject with at least one post-baseline value of the vital sign <test>.
alternatives.meaning: A post-baseline value is a non-missing result dated after the treatment start date. The set is a modified intent-to-treat set (mITT): a predefined part of the randomized set, still written to ITTFL.
